nodes.description: Manganese accumulation in the globus pallidus perturbs the basal ganglia-thalamocortical motor circuit, influencing the subthalamic nucleus and substantia nigra and thereby altering thalamic and cortical motor output. The result is an extrapyramidal, parkinsonism-like syndrome. This node is a partial conformer to the parkinsonism dopaminergic-degeneration module: it converges on basal-ganglia motor-circuit dysfunction and parkinsonism but, unlike idiopathic Parkinson disease, the predominant lesion is pallidal rather than nigrostriatal-dopaminergic, accounting for the characteristically poor levodopa response.
nodes.id: Basal Ganglia Circuit Dysfunction and Extrapyramidal Parkinsonism

nodes.description: Chronic inhalational or ingested manganese crosses into the CNS and accumulates preferentially in the basal ganglia, initially the globus pallidus and, with prolonged lower-level exposure, extending across the basal ganglia toward the substantia nigra pars compacta. This metal deposition (visible as T1 MRI hyperintensity) and the attendant oxidative stress are the initiating lesion of the disorder.

nodes.description: Manganese is an essential trace metal whose body burden is set by the balance of intestinal absorption against hepatobiliary excretion into the gut. Chronic overexposure, impaired biliary excretion (liver failure, cholestasis), or a route that bypasses first-pass hepatic clearance altogether (inhalation of welding fume and ore dust, or intravenous delivery in total parenteral nutrition) raises the systemic manganese burden that all downstream steps depend on. This node is where the exposure enters the mechanism.
nodes.id: Manganese Overexposure and Failure of Hepatobiliary Clearance

nodes.description: Divalent manganese drives hydrogen peroxide production in the mitochondrial fraction of microglia, and the effect is supported by the complex II substrate succinate and abolished by complex II inhibition. Complex I substrates do not support it and complex I inhibition does not abolish it, so the oxidative lesion of manganese is specifically complex II-dependent. The resulting microglial free-radical output in turn facilitates dopaminergic neurotoxicity.

nodes.description: Manganese is not freely diffusible: it enters cells through divalent-metal transporters (DMT1/SLC11A2, ZIP8/SLC39A8, ZIP14/SLC39A14) and is exported again by ferroportin and SLC30A10. Brain manganese therefore reflects the balance of these influx and efflux carriers rather than exposure alone, which is why iron deficiency (which competes for the same carriers) and loss of the SLC30A10 efflux transporter both raise brain manganese at unchanged exposure.
nodes.id: Transporter-Mediated Manganese Uptake into the Central Nervous System

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in SLC30A10 cause parkinsonism and dystonia with hypermanganesemia, polycythemia, and chronic liver disease.
evidence.snippet: SLC30A10 mutations cause a treatable recessive disease with pleomorphic phenotype, and provide compelling evidence that SLC30A10 plays a pivotal role in manganese transport
